newsitem.title: USA: Freeport net boosted by option trades.
newsitem.headline: Freeport net boosted by option trades.

text.p: Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc reported sharply higher first quarter earnings citing the benefits of its trading program and saying it had excellent operating results during the quarter.
Profits totaled $71.8 million in the quarter, nearly double the $36.1 million earned in 1996's first quarter.

Net income applicable to common stock of $62.5 million, or $0.31 per share, compared with $22.5 million, or $0.11 per share, last year after preferred dividends of $9.4 million in 1997 and $13.7 million in 1996. The company said the re-pricing of

"open" pounds at December 31, 1996; the sale of copper put option contracts and forward gold sales contracts collectively added $33.5 million to net income in the latest quarter, equal to $0.16 per share.

Quarterly sales volumes of Freeport's principal mining unit, P.T. Freeport Indonesia Co, were 256.1 million pounds of copper and 373,500 ounces of gold, 14 percent and 24 percent higher, respectively, than the 1996 quarter.
Second-quarter 1997 sales are projected to be slightly higher than first quarter levels, Freeport Copper said.

In February, PT-FI closed gold sales contracts covering 876,000 ounces of gold at an average price of $376.08 per ounce and realized $30.1 million cash, Freeport said. As a result, PT-FI will report gold revenues through August 1997 at a higher price than realized, but no longer has a forward gold sales position.
Freeport Copper said it will recognize revenues from closing forward gold sales contracts totaling $17.5 million in the second quarter and $6.0 million in the third quarter.
It said PT-FI has suspended its program of selling gold forward on a six-month basis but may reinstate the program.

During the third quarter of 1996, PT-FI sold all of its copper put option contracts. As a result, it is reporting copper revenues through June 30, 1997, at a higher price than realized under its copper concentrate sales contracts, but PT-FI no longer has a floor price on any of its copper sales.

For the first quarter of 1997, PT-FI recognized $23.0 million of revenues from the sale of the contracts, before costs of $5.3 million to acquire the contracts, which added $8.6 million, or $0.04 per share, to net income.
PT-FI's average realized copper price in the first quarter of 1997 was $1.13 per pound.
Through March 31, 1997, it has recognized $74.1 million of revenues from the sale of the contracts. It will recognize revenues from the sale totaling $23.1 million in the second quarter of 1997.

PT-FI's copper concentrate sales agreements provide for provisional pricing at the time of shipment with final settlement based on the average LME price for a specified future month. Copper revenues on provisionally priced "open" pounds are adjusted monthly based on then current prices.
First-quarter 1997 Freeport Coper revenues include favorable adjustments to December 31, 1996, open sales of $36.9 million, adding $18.0 million, or $0.09 per share, to net income.

At March 31, 1997, copper sales totaling 317.5 million pounds, recorded at an average price of $1.05 per pound, remained to be finally priced. About 60 percent of these "open" pounds are expected to be finally priced during the second quarter with most of the rest during the third quarter.
The benefits of higher gold credits and lower unit royalty costs were partially offset by higher unit site production and delivery costs and treatment charges.

Freeport said the higher unit site production costs primarily relate to operating the first phase of the enhanced infrastructure program, including Kuala Kencana, which was completed during the second half of 1996. Average unit site production and delivery costs for 1997 are currently estimated to approximate the 1996 average as sales of copper are expected to increase and therefore reduce unit costs in the second half of the year.

Atlantic Copper Holding SA recorded operating income of $3.7 million for the quarter compared with a loss of $4.2 million in the 1996 period, reflecting higher volumes and lower cathode cash production costs resulting from the Spanish operation's expansion completed in mid-1996. Higher unit treatment charges also benefited Atlantic's results. The effect of an equivalent change in treatment charges on PT-FI and Atlantic would now be largely offset in Freeport Copper's consolidated financial results.
